nodes.label: Module 9 — Clinical Assessments Suite
nodes.rationale: Where M8 owns the narrative of what happened, M9 owns the numbers that quantify decline and their longitudinal series — the most-asked-for artifact in a hospice CMS survey. The bet is that the alert, trend, reconstruction and consent gating are the differentiated half, not per-form ergonomics.

nodes.label: Shared clinical_assessment Base Table + per-scale data jsonb (D1)
nodes.rationale: One hot table preserves an efficient latest(patientId, scaleType) index, keeps partitioning trivial at one monthly cadence, and lets M14/M22/M28 read a uniform shape; per-scale TypeBox restores the strict validation a generic table would lose. One-table-per-scale means 14 partition sets and a fragile union view.

nodes.label: Server-Authoritative Score Computation (D6)
nodes.rationale: Scores feed alerts, IDG packets and M10's HOPE items; a client-trusted score would let a misbehaving or compromised client suppress significant-change alerts by under-scoring. Computing once server-side means chart, trend, FHIR export and CTI narrative all show the same canonical number.

nodes.label: Significant-Change Detection with Platform Floors, Tenant-Tighten-Only (D2)
nodes.rationale: The PAINAD/ESAS-r/Braden/Morse evidence base sets a clinical floor below which silence is unsafe; a loosened threshold would let a tenant suppress alerts the platform considers mandatory. Tightening is the tenant choosing to be more cautious. Detection runs inside the recordAssessment transaction.

nodes.label: ScaleSeriesProvider / LatestAssessmentProvider Seams (D7)
nodes.rationale: Two interfaces are M9's entire public surface, so M9 can swap to a materialized backing later without a single consumer changing; direct table reads would couple every consumer to M9's partition and RLS internals.

nodes.label: Scale License Registry with Form-Gating (D3)
nodes.rationale: PPS, FAST, GDS, Braden and Morse IP holders require per-organization licensure evidence; the cleanest legal posture is refusing to capture new measurements when the license lapses while preserving clinical history recorded under a prior active license. Most vendors ship these as fields and trust the tenant — a recurring small survey finding.

nodes.label: Discipline × Scale Eligibility Typed Matrix (D8)
nodes.rationale: CoP ties certain assessments to specific disciplines; encoding it as a typed matrix surfaces violations in CI rather than at runtime. Per-tenant configurability was rejected because it invites tenants to weaken a CoP-driven boundary.

nodes.label: Append-Only Correction-of-Record Amendment (D9)
nodes.rationale: A correction inserts a new row referencing corrects_assessment_id and a trigger marks the prior row superseded; update-in-place destroys the original value's row identity and soft-delete-plus-reinsert loses the explicit 'this corrects that' linkage.

nodes.label: 42 CFR Part 2 Gates Disclosure, Not Record Creation (D10 / M09-F05)
nodes.rationale: The v0.2 design blocking AIMS writes without a release was reversed: Part 2 governs disclosure distinctly from HIPAA and does not bar the treating program from recording SUD data. Gating creation would suppress clinically necessary tardive-dyskinesia surveillance; the obligation attaches when the record leaves the treating program, so the gate moves to every read/FHIR/portal/AoD egress boundary and M39-down now fails disclosure closed rather than blocking writes.

nodes.label: Read-Time Trend Computation, Materialization Deferred (D4)
nodes.rationale: One patient × one scale × 90 days is rarely more than ~30 rows, so a materialized view would add replication lag, an invalidation surface and a second source of truth for IDG and HOPE reads; read-time computation also lets corrections take effect immediately.

nodes.label: Nullable source_encounter_id Forward Seam (D5)
nodes.rationale: M9 has standalone clinical value (telephonic check-ins, IDG-only review, retrospective paper entry), and blocking M9 on M8 would block M7 → IDG which already consumes LatestAssessmentProvider. Synthesizing a virtual encounter would add a ghost row M8 later has to reconcile.
